sentences.zh: 我当时在和一个不太熟的女人聊天，我们聊得很投机，谈到了政治，还有我们对某些事情的看法。

sentences.en: So I guess it was like immigration, climate change, and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是移民、气候变化之类的话题吧。

sentences.en: And this woman was on board with all of the democratic ideals.
sentences.zh: 这个女人完全赞同民主党的所有理念。

sentences.en: And then I mentioned Hillary Clinton, and she said, oh, I hate her.
sentences.zh: 然后我提到了希拉里·克林顿，她说，哦，我讨厌她。

sentences.en: And I said, really?
sentences.zh: 我说，真的吗？

sentences.en: Because she's the one who stands for all of these things that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 因为她正是主张我们刚才讨论的这些观点的人啊。

sentences.en: Nope, nope, I can't stand her.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我就是受不了她。

sentences.en: I said, well, why don't you like her?
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你为什么不喜欢她？

sentences.en: Oh, I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不知道。

sentences.en: I said, is it because she's an aggressive woman?
sentences.zh: 我说，是因为她是一个强势的女人吗？

sentences.en: Is she too aggressive?
sentences.zh: 她太咄咄逼人了吗？

sentences.en: Is she too loud?
sentences.zh: 她声音太大了吗？

sentences.en: Does she express herself too much?
sentences.zh: 她表现得太激进了吗？

sentences.en: And her reply was, no, I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 她的回答是，不，我不知道为什么。

sentences.en: So like a minute later, I mentioned Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 所以在大概一分钟后，我提到了伊丽莎白·沃伦。

sentences.en: She said, oh, I can't stand her, Rita.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，我受不了她，丽塔。

sentences.en: So I was like, she agrees with you about everything.
sentences.zh: 于是我说，她对所有事情的看法都跟你一样啊。

sentences.en: All the things that you're saying you believe in, she is promoting.
sentences.zh: 你所说的那些你深信不疑的事情，全都是她在力推的。

sentences.en: No, well, I can't stand her.
sentences.zh: 不，反正我就是受不了她。

sentences.en: So I know.
sentences.zh: 所以我懂的。

sentences.en: I mean, I've been a woman my whole life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我当了一辈子女人。

sentences.en: So I know very well that that is the reason.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常清楚，这就是原因所在。

sentences.en: Even women will vote against women because they're women.
sentences.zh: 甚至连女性也会因为对方是女性而投票反对女性。

sentences.en: There are people out there who have this idea that you're not trustworthy, that they don't like you for some reason.
sentences.zh: 总会有人觉得你不可信，或者出于某种原因就是不喜欢你。

sentences.en: What is that about, in your opinion?
sentences.zh: 依你之见，这到底是为什么？

sentences.en: You know, Joy, obviously I've thought a lot about it because I don't like to hear it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，乔伊，显然我对此思考了很久，因为我实在不想听到这种说法。

sentences.en: So I need to figure out what's behind it.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须弄清楚这背后的原因。

sentences.en: You know, I am perhaps a more serious person, a more reserved person than is kind of in the public arena these days.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，相比于如今活跃在公众视野中的人，我可能是一个更严肃、更内敛的人。

sentences.en: So I think people then say, well, you know, she's serious, she's reserved.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为人们就会说，嗯，你看，她很严肃，她很内敛。

sentences.en: Can I really like her?
sentences.zh: 我真的能喜欢她吗？

sentences.en: But what is inauthentic?
sentences.zh: 但什么才叫不真实？

sentences.en: What's inauthentic?
sentences.zh: 什么叫不真实？

sentences.en: I don't understand that.
sentences.zh: 我不明白这意思。

sentences.en: I don't understand that.
sentences.zh: 我真的不明白。

sentences.en: Because I've been pretty much the same person my entire life, for better or worse, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我这辈子几乎一直是同一个人，无论是好是坏，对吧？

sentences.en: Clinton losing made a difference.
sentences.zh: 克林顿的落败确实产生了影响。

sentences.en: Clinton losing did make it harder for me to think that a woman could win.
sentences.zh: 克林顿的落败确实让我更难相信女性能够赢得大选。

sentences.en: So this year, when Elizabeth Warren announces that she's running, Lynn has mixed feelings.
sentences.zh: 所以今年，当伊丽莎白·沃伦宣布参选时，琳恩的心情很复杂。

sentences.en: I love that people were getting to know her all across the country.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴全国各地的人们开始认识她。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: My name's Raelynn.
sentences.zh: 我叫雷琳。

sentences.en: Hi, Raelynn.
sentences.zh: 嗨，雷琳。

sentences.en: I was wondering if there was ever a time in your life where somebody you really looked up to
sentences.zh: 我想知道，在你的人生中，有没有那么一段时间，你非常崇拜的人

sentences.en: maybe didn't accept you as much and how you dealt with that.
sentences.zh: 可能并没有那么接纳你，你是如何处理这种情况的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: My mother and I had very different views of how to build a future.
sentences.zh: 我和我母亲在如何建立未来这方面有着非常不同的观点。

sentences.en: She wanted me to marry well, and I really tried.
sentences.zh: 她希望我找个好人家嫁了，我真的很努力去试过了。

sentences.en: And it just didn't work out.
sentences.zh: 但结果就是行不通。

sentences.en: But I also know it was the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 不过我也知道，坚持自我才是对的。

sentences.en: And sometimes you just got to do what's right inside.
sentences.zh: 有时你只需遵从内心的指引去做正确的事。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: You've got to take care of yourself first and do this.
sentences.zh: 你必须首先照顾好自己，然后把这件事做好。

sentences.en: Give me a hug.
sentences.zh: 给我一个拥抱。

sentences.en: And it was a pleasure for me to see that, although I was a little bit, you know, worried.
sentences.zh: 看到这一幕我感到非常高兴，尽管我当时还有点，你知道的，担心。

sentences.en: In the wake of her third-place finish in Iowa and fourth-place finish in New Hampshire,
sentences.zh: 在艾奥瓦州初选获得第三名、在新罕布什尔州初选获得第四名之后，

sentences.en: Warren said, my job is to persiSt.
sentences.zh: 沃伦表示：“我的工作就是坚持到底。”

sentences.en: But persisting and winning are two very different things.
sentences.zh: 但坚持和获胜是两码事。

sentences.en: Senator Elizabeth Warren, she came in fifth place in South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦参议员在南卡罗来纳州仅名列第五。

sentences.en: Senator Elizabeth Warren trailing in fourth place.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦参议员目前在第四位苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: I think the biggest question that Elizabeth Warren has to answer is, where does she win?
sentences.zh: 我认为伊丽莎白·沃伦必须回答的最大问题是：她究竟能在哪里取胜？

sentences.en: Lynn voted early in Massachusetts for Senator Warren.
sentences.zh: 琳恩在马萨诸塞州提前投给了沃伦参议员。

sentences.en: But in the days leading up to Super Tuesday, she's questioning her vote and wondering if she did the right thing.
sentences.zh: 但在超级星期二来临前的几天里，她开始对自己的投票产生质疑，琢磨着自己到底有没有做对。

sentences.en: But I didn't feel—I didn't feel bad that I had already voted for her at all.
sentences.zh: 但我并不觉得——一点也不觉得投给她有什么不对。

sentences.en: Because that, you know, like she said, vote with your heart.
sentences.zh: 因为就像她说的，凭你的内心去投票。

sentences.en: And she was my heart.
sentences.zh: 而她就是我心中的首选。

sentences.en: Did you know anyone personally in your life who were for Warren and then jumped ship?
sentences.zh: 你身边有没有人本来支持沃伦，后来却临阵倒戈的？

sentences.en: Yes, my cousin Kathleen.
sentences.zh: 有，我的表姐凯瑟琳。

sentences.en: Raising her hand.
sentences.zh: 她正举着手呢。

sentences.en: Actually, as soon as Buttigieg and Klobuchar backed Biden, and I was kind of waiting to see how it all kind of shook out a little bit,
sentences.zh: 其实，就在布蒂吉格和克洛布查支持拜登之后，我当时还在观望局势会怎么发展，

sentences.en: I voted for Biden because we have to stop Sanders, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 我投票给了拜登，因为在我看来，我们必须阻止桑德斯。

sentences.en: But I would have voted for Warren because I voted for Hillary.
sentences.zh: 但我本来是会投给沃伦的，因为我投给过希拉里。

sentences.en: As Kathleen is talking, Tom nods and raises his hand.
sentences.zh: 正当凯瑟琳在说话时，汤姆点着头并举起了手。

sentences.en: Yeah, did you raise your hand, too?
sentences.zh: 对，你也举手了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, actually, as the sole old white guy in the room, I too did vote for Biden, though.
sentences.zh: 对，其实作为房间里唯一的年长白人老头，我也确实投给了拜登。

sentences.en: I love Elizabeth Warren, and she would have made an extraordinarily wonderful president.
sentences.zh: 我深爱伊丽莎白·沃伦，她本可以成为一位极其卓越的总统。

sentences.en: By the time Massachusetts was voting, if she looked more electable, if she was a frontrunner, you all would have stuck with it.
sentences.zh: 到马萨诸塞州投票的时候，如果她看起来更有胜算，如果她处于领跑地位，你们大家都会坚持支持她的。

sentences.en: Yeah, you bet.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 绝对会的，没错。

sentences.en: Did you see when she, you know, obviously she comes out and talks at her house.
sentences.zh: 你看到她，你知道的，显然她从家里出来发表讲话的那次吗？

sentences.en: Did you see that?
sentences.zh: 你看到了吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，看到了。

sentences.en: I was here in the living room.
sentences.zh: 我当时就在客厅里。

sentences.en: I was in my own living room listening to it, watching, and yeah, I cried through the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 我坐在自己的客厅里听着、看着，是的，我全程都在哭。

sentences.en: It's heartbreaking.
sentences.zh: 这太让人心碎了。

sentences.en: Do you remember something she said that day that stuck with you or maybe caused you to, like, feel that emotion?
sentences.zh: 你还记得她那天说过的话中，有什么触动了你，或者让你产生了那种情绪吗？

sentences.en: Well, one of the things was that, you know how she talked about the pinky swear that she does with the little kids?
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一件事就是，你知道她提到过她跟小孩子们拉钩的事吗？

sentences.en: The first time I met her, which was way back when, before she was elected senator for the first time, she was doing that with little girls that were there.
sentences.zh: 我第一次见到她是在很久以前，在她第一次当选参议员之前，她当时就在和在场的小女孩们做这个动作。

sentences.en: What is the pinky swear?
sentences.zh: 什么是拉钩？

sentences.en: Was she promising girls?
sentences.zh: 她是在向女孩们承诺什么吗？

sentences.en: She said that girls can be president.
sentences.zh: 她说女孩也能当总统。

sentences.en: She gets right down to their level.
sentences.zh: 她直接蹲到和孩子们一样的高度。

sentences.en: She gets right down to their eye level and talks to the girls like that.
sentences.zh: 她降到和女孩们平视的视线高度，就这样跟女孩子们说话。

sentences.en: The race is now down to two guys.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选现在缩减为两个男人之间的较量。

sentences.en: After starting with such a diverse field, gender, racial, all of that, how does it feel for it to be down to two men when you had four women senators at the start,
sentences.zh: 最初的参选阵容如此多元，涉及性别、种族等方方面面，而当最初有四位女参议员——

sentences.en: all of whom you liked?
sentences.zh: 而且你们全都喜欢她们——现在却只剩两个男人，你作何感想？

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我懂的。

sentences.en: It's sick, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这真让人恶心，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's, you know, it was almost inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这，你知道的，几乎是不可避免的。

sentences.en: I think people are, not panicked, but I think that people are very, very concerned that we have to beat Trump.
sentences.zh: 我想人们倒也不是恐慌，但我认为大家非常、非常担心我们必须击败特朗普。

sentences.en: But why does the feeling of need to beat Trump then translate to men?
sentences.zh: 但为什么“必须击败特朗普”这种迫切感最终会转化为只能选男性？

sentences.en: So you're saying, I think a lot of people are scared.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，我认为很多人都在害怕。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people just want to beat Trump.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人只是想要击败特朗普。

sentences.en: And that's why it came down to two men.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么最终变成了两个男人之间的对决。

sentences.en: What is necessarily male about those qualities?
sentences.zh: 这些特质里有什么必然是属于男性的吗？

sentences.en: Because there are so many people in the country that just would not vote for a woman, like that woman that I was talking about before.
sentences.zh: 因为全国有那么多人根本不会投票给女性，就像我刚才提到的那个女人一样。

sentences.en: And we really feel the need to prevail this time, especially.
sentences.zh: 而且我们特别觉得这一次我们必须赢。

sentences.en: So the idea that a woman candidate is a risk because of other people's or the country's sexism.
sentences.zh: 所以，由于别人或整个国家的性别歧视，导致女候选人被认为是一种风险。

sentences.en: Yes, that's how I feel.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我的感受。

sentences.en: It's a terrible thing to have to feel, but I do feel that way.
sentences.zh: 有这种感觉是很糟糕的一件事，但我的确这么觉得。

sentences.en: Right now.
sentences.zh: 就目前而言。

sentences.en: I don't think it's always going to be like that, but I think it's the way it is right now.
sentences.zh: 我不认为情况会一直这样下去，但我觉得现在就是这个样子。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: You can go skiing now.
sentences.zh: 你现在可以去滑雪了。

sentences.en: Oh, good.
sentences.zh: 哦，太好了。

sentences.en: I'm sorry you can't come with us.
sentences.zh: 真遗憾你不能跟我们一起去。

sentences.en: That was too bad.
sentences.zh: 太可惜了。

sentences.en: Tell us where you're going.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们你们要去哪里。

sentences.en: Warren, Vermont.
sentences.zh: 佛蒙特州的沃伦镇。

sentences.en: It's very funny because we have our ski place right next to our daughter and son-in-law in Warren, Vermont.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我们在佛蒙特州沃伦镇的滑雪屋就在我们女儿和女婿家隔壁。

sentences.en: And our son-in-law's parents live in Warren, Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 而我们女婿的父母住在罗德岛州的沃伦。

sentences.en: A Warren household to the end.
sentences.zh: 真是一个从头到尾都和“沃伦”结缘的家庭。

sentences.en: It's one voter's view that sexism is what consumed the Elizabeth Warren campaign.
sentences.zh: 有选民认为，正是性别歧视毁了伊丽莎白·沃伦的竞选活动。

sentences.en: And certainly, that's one that's popular among her most diehard supporters.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种观点在她的铁杆支持者中非常流行。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering, is this the view inside her own campaign?
sentences.zh: 但我想知道，这也是她竞选团队内部的看法吗？

sentences.en: Do they think that the barriers that gender placed on them were too big to overcome?
sentences.zh: 他们是否认为性别施加在身上的重重壁垒过于巨大，以至于无法克服？

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App吗？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在机会来了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在该App内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》App，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: The same day we met with Lynn, we headed to the Charlestown neighborhood of Boston, to Elizabeth Warren's campaign headquarters.
sentences.zh: 就在我们与琳恩会面的同一天，我们前往波士顿的查尔斯敦社区，来到了伊丽莎白·沃伦的竞选总部。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a warehouse-y building, nondescript, very on brand.
sentences.zh: 那有点像一个仓库式的建筑，平平无奇，非常符合他们的风格。

sentences.en: There is a Dunkin' Donuts right across the street.
sentences.zh: 街对面就有一家唐恩都乐（Dunkin' Donuts）。

sentences.en: To meet with someone who's worked for the Warren campaign from the start.
sentences.zh: 去见一位从一开始就为沃伦竞选团队工作的人。

sentences.en: I'm Kristen Orthman, the Communications Director for Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 我是克里斯滕·奥思曼，伊丽莎白·沃伦的传讯总监。

sentences.en: As Communications Director, Kristen's in charge of trying to best translate the candidate to the rest of the country, particularly through the media.
sentences.zh: 作为传讯总监，克里斯滕负责将候选人的理念尽可能向全国各地进行最佳传达，特别是通过媒体渠道。

sentences.en: And over the course of this campaign, we got to know each other pretty well.
sentences.zh: 在这场竞选的过程中，我们渐渐变得相当熟悉。

sentences.en: Now that the campaign has ended, I'm wondering whether Kristen will speak more candidly about what went wrong,
sentences.zh: 既然竞选已经结束，我在想，克里斯滕是否会更坦诚地谈谈哪里出了问题，

sentences.en: and about what role gender specifically played in the campaign's demise.
sentences.zh: 以及性别具体在竞选的失败中扮演了什么角色。

sentences.en: Is there something different about planning communications and media for women politicians?
sentences.zh: 为女性政治家规划宣传和媒体策略，有什么不同之处吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: In what way?
sentences.zh: 在哪些方面？

sentences.en: I think that there can be more caution when you're working for a woman because you're viewing things through the lens of much more of how will this be perceived.
sentences.zh: 我认为当你为女性工作时，可能会更加谨慎，因为你是通过“这会被如何看待”这种大得多的镜头来审视事物。

sentences.en: And I think I have an appreciation for the challenges of the Clinton presidential campaign, probably now, than I did when I first started.
sentences.zh: 我想，比起我刚开始的时候，我现在大概更能体会到克林顿总统竞选所面临的挑战了。

sentences.en: In what way?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: I think that the fact that there were stories when Elizabeth first ran, there was an infamous one, like the day she announced.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，事实上在伊丽莎白刚参选时就有过一些报道，有一个声名狼藉的例子，就像她宣布参选的那天。

sentences.en: This is December 31st, 2018, when Warren first announced her intentions to seek the presidency.
sentences.zh: 那是2018年12月31日，沃伦首次宣布竞选总统意向的时候。

sentences.en: Talking about, like, I think it was the likability factor, her versus Hillary, because there were two women who ran for president who,
sentences.zh: 讨论的好像是，我觉得是好感度因素，她与希拉里的对比，因为有两位女性参选总统，她们是，

sentences.en: two white women who ran for president that had blonde hair.
sentences.zh: 两位参选总统的白人女性，都留着金发。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess I'm not quite sure what else warranted necessarily that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我其实不太确定还有什么其他原因一定需要那样做。

sentences.en: So when it becomes clear she's running for president, how forefront of mind was gender and the need to define her on her own outside of Clinton or whatever terms?
sentences.zh: 所以，当她显然要竞选总统时，性别以及需要在克林顿或其他任何条条框框之外重新定义她的需求，在多大程度上是当务之急？

sentences.en: I think when you're running for president, male, female, you have to be yourself.
sentences.zh: 我认为当你竞选总统时，无论是男是女，你都必须做你自己。

sentences.en: So what I was always, and what our team and her always wanted to make sure is you're showing what you would hope is the truest version of yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直以来，以及我们的团队和她本人，始终想要确保的是，你要展现出你所期望的最真实版本的自己。

sentences.en: One of the critiques of the Clinton campaign, fair or not, was that many voters felt like they never really knew her authentic self.
sentences.zh: 对克林顿竞选团队的批评之一，无论公允与否，是许多选民觉得他们从未真正了解她真实的一面。

sentences.en: That there was a barrier between candidate and voter, built up over all those years in the public eye.
sentences.zh: 在候选人与选民之间存在着一道屏障，这是在公众视线中历经多年筑起来的。

sentences.en: So Kristen and her team tried to go in the opposite direction, to distinguish Warren, both from Clinton, but also from everyone else.
sentences.zh: 因此，克里斯滕和她的团队试图朝相反的方向努力，将沃伦与克林顿区分开来，同时也与其他人区分开来。

sentences.en: You know, she runs out on stage.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她一路小跑上台。

sentences.en: She dances.
sentences.zh: 她跳舞。

sentences.en: She stays for hours for photos.
sentences.zh: 她留下来合影好几个小时。

sentences.en: So we just finished our event here in New York City, and I got a lot of notes and a can.
sentences.zh: 我们刚在纽约市结束了活动，我收到了很多便条和一个罐子。

sentences.en: She is just like the compassionate and joyful person that I know behind the scenes, was the person that was on a town hall stage.
sentences.zh: 她在幕后展现出的那种富有同情心和快乐的个性，正是站在市民大会舞台上的那个人。

sentences.en: Or the, like, fighter that I've also seen behind the scenes and that many people saw, whether in the hearing room or otherwise, was the person on the debate stage.
sentences.zh: 或者我也曾在幕后以及许多人所看到的那种斗士形象，无论是在听证会上还是其他地方，就是辩论舞台上的那个人。

sentences.en: There is a vulnerability that comes with that, being a female candidate versus being a male candidate.
sentences.zh: 与男性候选人相比，作为女性候选人会带来一种脆弱感。

sentences.en: I always was thinking through the risks in that, because I just knew that the mistakes that, I'm using quotes because I don't always think they were,
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考其中的风险，因为我很清楚那些错误，我用引号是因为我并不总是认为它们是错误，

sentences.en: but they were perceived as mistakes that female candidates make.
sentences.zh: 但它们被视为女性候选人所犯的错误。

sentences.en: It's like a higher bar.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个更高的标准。

sentences.en: But to her, these risks were necessary components of running an authentic campaign.
sentences.zh: 但对她来说，这些风险是开展一场真实竞选的必要组成部分。

sentences.en: Let's do the things that have now become, like, signatures of the, were signatures of the campaign.
sentences.zh: 让我们去做那些现在已经成为标志的事情，也就是竞选活动标志的事情。

sentences.en: It's like, well, okay, she's running for president to say something and do something, so let's start doing that.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，好吧，她竞选总统是为了表达某种观点并做些事情，那我们就开始做吧。

sentences.en: 2020 Democratic presidential candidate Elizabeth Warren is leading the pack when it comes to policy proposals.
sentences.zh: 2020年民主党总统候选人伊丽莎白·沃伦在政策提案方面遥遥领先。

sentences.en: So I've got a plan for 3.2 million new housing units in America.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一个在美国新建320万套住房的计划。

sentences.en: I've got a plan to put 800 billion new federal dollars into our public schools.
sentences.zh: 我有一个向我们的公立学校投入8000亿美元新联邦资金的计划。

sentences.en: Thank you, Senator.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，参议员。

sentences.en: Wait, student loan debt, I got a, I got a plan for that.
sentences.zh: 等等，学生贷款债务，我有一个，我有一个解决这个问题的计划。

sentences.en: She became known as the I have a plan for that candidate.
sentences.zh: 她被称为“我对此有个计划”的候选人。

sentences.en: The I have a plan for that just kind of happened organically.
sentences.zh: “我对此有个计划”这句话基本上是自然而然产生的。

sentences.en: Time magazine put it on the cover and that's kind of when it became more of a thing.
sentences.zh: 《时代》杂志把它放到了封面，大概也就是从那时起，这变得更加火了。

sentences.en: I think it happened, like, grassroots level before that.
sentences.zh: 我想在此之前它就已经在基层层面发生了。

sentences.en: People started talking about it because we were doing it, like.
sentences.zh: 人们开始谈论它，因为我们一直在这样做，比如说。

sentences.en: There was, like, a whole meme section of, like, Warren playing.
sentences.zh: 当时甚至有一个关于沃伦玩梗的整个板块。

sentences.en: That's what I mean, is, like, yeah, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的意思，就是，是的，没错，完全没错。

sentences.en: And by the end of last fall, Warren has crossed into frontrunner status.
sentences.zh: 到去年秋天结束时，沃伦已经跨入了领跑者的地位。

sentences.en: He's leading in some national polls.
sentences.zh: 她在一些全国民调中领先。

sentences.en: But this is also about the time that I noticed the shift in the race.
sentences.zh: 但这也是我注意到比赛发生转变的时间点。

sentences.en: The primary change from a contest to ideas to one of just an obsession about who could win.
sentences.zh: 初选从一场理念的较量变成了对谁能赢的执念。

sentences.en: Do you think that's true?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是真的吗？

sentences.en: I think the primary campaign has always been about who can win.
sentences.zh: 我认为初选一直都是关于谁能赢。

sentences.en: How does that impact the women specifically who are running?
sentences.zh: 这具体对参选的女性产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: I do think I, like, sort of need distance in order to fully formulate.
sentences.zh: 我确实觉得我需要一些距离，以便能够完全形成看法。

sentences.en: But I don't think there's any question that electability was viewed through a lens that probably hurt the women candidates because there was a perception that after 2016,
sentences.zh: 但我认为毫无疑问，对胜选可能性的看法是通过一个很可能伤害了女性候选人的有色眼镜来看待的，因为有一种看法认为，在2016年之后，

sentences.en: even though the female candidate got 3 million more votes, is a woman not electable?
sentences.zh: 尽管女性候选人多获得了300万张选票，难道女性就无法胜选吗？

sentences.en: And she has said before publicly that she would hear that from people in the early states, like, I'm worried about who can beat Trump.
sentences.zh: 她以前曾公开说过，她在早期几个州的选民那里听到过这种说法，比如，我担心谁能击败特朗普。

sentences.en: But I don't think all of a sudden, in October, it was like, let's make this primary about who's going to beat Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为突然之间，在10月份的时候，就变成：让我们把这次初选变成关于谁能击败唐纳德·特朗普的比赛。

sentences.en: Like, that's what it's been.
sentences.zh: 听着，事情一直就是这样的。

sentences.en: That's what it's been.
sentences.zh: 事情一直就是这样的。

sentences.en: I would largely agree.
sentences.zh: 我基本上表示赞同。

sentences.en: Certainly, electability has never been far from mind for most Democratic voters.
sentences.zh: 当然，对绝大多数民主党选民来说，胜选可能性一直是挥之不去的考量。

sentences.en: But as more and more people tuned into the race, particularly around this time in the late fall, it shifted its tone.
sentences.zh: 但随着越来越多的人开始关注这场竞选，特别是在深秋的这个时间段，它的基调发生了变化。

sentences.en: Policy ideas took a backseat to that electability question.
sentences.zh: 政策理念退居其次，让位于关于胜选可能性的问题。

sentences.en: And the candidates who had most clearly articulated their path to victory started to rise, while Elizabeth Warren started to fall.
sentences.zh: 那些最清晰阐述了通往胜利之路的候选人开始崛起，而伊丽莎白·沃伦则开始下滑。

sentences.en: This coincided with rival candidates like Pete Buttigieg and Amy Klobuchar increasingly casting Warren's campaign as out of touch with the mainstream Democratic Party and the real general election risk.
sentences.zh: 这与皮特·布蒂吉格和埃米·克洛布查尔等竞争对手不谋而合，他们越来越将沃伦的竞选描绘为脱离主流民主党以及构成真实大选风险的存在。

sentences.en: And so, to respond to that scrutiny, the Warren campaign tries to reposition itself as a unity candidate, someone who can actually bring all sides together.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了应对这种审视，沃伦的竞选团队试图把自己重新定位为团结型候选人，一个真正能将各方凝聚在一起的人。

sentences.en: There's some time during the kind of, like, unity candidate phase, where I did feel like it was different from the fight that we had heard before.
sentences.zh: 在所谓团结型候选人阶段的某个时期，我确实觉得它与我们以前听到的那种斗争有所不同。

sentences.en: How do you square those two versions that we did see just this year?
sentences.zh: 你如何调和我们在今年刚刚看到的这两种不同的形象？

sentences.en: Um, I mean, I think you can both—unity doesn't mean not fighting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我认为你可以兼具两者——团结并不意味着不抗争。

sentences.en: I never didn't think she was herself.
sentences.zh: 我从未觉得她不是她自己。

sentences.en: Take us into, like, debate prep, for instance.
sentences.zh: 把我们带入辩论准备阶段，举个例子。

sentences.en: Like, are you sitting there thinking, we have to package a candidate and there are concerns about how she'll be perceived if she attacks too much or attacks too little?
sentences.zh: 比如说，你会不会坐在那里想：我们必须把候选人包装好，如果她攻击太多或攻击太少，人们会担心她会被如何看待？

sentences.en: Like, how much is gender a concern as you are thinking about the big national combative moments?
sentences.zh: 当你思考那些激烈的全国交锋时刻时，性别在多大程度上是一个顾虑？

sentences.en: You know, I don't want to make a big statement saying it's easier for men to attack than women.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我不想发表宏论说男性攻击比女性攻击更容易。

sentences.en: I do think that there are probably greater consequences to a failed attack by a female than a failed attack by a male.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，女性发起攻击失败所带来的后果，可能要比男性攻击失败更大。

sentences.en: Because, obviously, she had a debate performance a couple, two debates ago, where she, you know, she was doing some level of contrast with Mayor Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，她在两场辩论前的一次辩论中表现出色，当时她，你知道的，她与彭博市长进行了一定程度的对比。

sentences.en: And—
sentences.zh: 然后——

sentences.en: Other statement.
sentences.zh: 另一份声明。

sentences.en: I'd like to talk about who we're running againSt.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈我们的竞争对手是谁。

sentences.en: A billionaire who calls women fat broads and horse-faced lesbians.
sentences.zh: 一个称女性为肥胖三八和马脸女同性恋的亿万富翁。

sentences.en: And, no, I'm not talking about Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 不，我说的不是唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: I'm talking about Mayor Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 我指的是彭博市长。

sentences.en: Democrats are not— She was really strong.
sentences.zh: 民主党人没有——她真的很强硬。

sentences.en: She was tough.
sentences.zh: 她很强悍。

sentences.en: And she was dynamic.
sentences.zh: 而且她很有活力。

sentences.en: Democrats take a huge risk if we just substitute one arrogant billionaire for another.
sentences.zh: 如果我们只是用一个傲慢的亿万富翁取代另一个傲慢的亿万富翁，民主党人将承担巨大的风险。

sentences.en: This country has worked— They were contrasting with each other.
sentences.zh: 这个国家已经运作了——他们在互相进行对比。

sentences.en: And I think, overall, it was agreed upon that she did well in that exchange.
sentences.zh: 我认为总的来说，大家一致认为她在这次交锋中表现不错。

sentences.en: But this came in Nevada, after two straight disappointing finishes, in Iowa and New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 但这是在内华达州发生的，此前她在爱荷华州和新罕布什尔州连续两次取得了令人失望的成绩。

sentences.en: Just—I mean, if we're just going to take Nevada, I feel like that is a reason to ask why then and not previously.
sentences.zh: 只是——我的意思是，如果我们只看内华达州，我觉得这有理由让人去问为什么是当时而不是之前。

sentences.en: Was it—were you all in rooms saying, well, we can't attack yet?
sentences.zh: 是不是——你们当时都在房间里说，好吧，我们还不能攻击？

sentences.en: But, you know, one of the things I remember from the second this campaign started was the way that supporters were so eager to see her, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，从这场竞选一开始我就记得的一件事，就是支持者们极其渴望看到她，你知道的，

sentences.en: cut down the Bidens and the Bernies and everyone else.
sentences.zh: 击败拜登、伯尼以及其他所有人。

sentences.en: It really didn't get that payoff until Nevada.
sentences.zh: 直到内华达州，这种期待才真正得到了回报。

sentences.en: So, I, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，我，有点，

sentences.en: kind of reject the premise of your question because I think that you can be both advocating for yourself and creating contrast in ways that are not—that don't always need to be how it happened in Nevada.
sentences.zh: 有点反感你问题中的前提，因为我认为你既可以为自己发声，又可以进行对比，而这些方式并不一定非要——并不一定需要像在内华达州那样发生。

sentences.en: Senator Warren, what did you think when Senator Sanders told you a woman could not win the election?
sentences.zh: 沃伦参议员，当桑德斯参议员告诉你女性无法赢得大选时，你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: I disagreed.
sentences.zh: 我不同意。

sentences.en: Bernie is my friend, and I am not here to try to fight with Bernie.
sentences.zh: 伯尼是我的朋友，我来这里不是为了和伯尼争吵。

sentences.en: But look—
sentences.zh: 但听着——

sentences.en: Now, someone say—and this is what I heard frequently from reporters—oh, you guys are doing subtle contraSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，有人说——这也是我经常从记者那里听到的——哦，你们在进行微妙的对比。

sentences.en: People don't get that.
sentences.zh: 人们不懂这个。

sentences.en: People don't know that.
sentences.zh: 人们不了解这个。

sentences.en: Like, I don't—I don't necessarily agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得——我并不一定赞同这种说法。

sentences.en: I think that you're always looking at the bar of how do we balance advocating for yourself and your ideas versus contrasting with other people.
sentences.zh: 我认为你总是在权衡这样一个标准：我们如何在为自己及自己的理念辩护与同其他人进行对比之间找到平衡？

sentences.en: You characterize Warren as contrasting with Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 你将沃伦的行为描述为与彭博进行对比。

sentences.en: Others might characterize that as she was attacking Bloomberg or going after Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能会将其描述为她在攻击彭博或针对彭博。

sentences.en: Um, and I wonder—yeah, I wonder if, like, in your role,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想知道——是的，我想知道，在你的角色中，

sentences.en: you're—you're choosing your words carefully because you know that male politicians are treated differently or characterized differently than female politicians.
sentences.zh: 你是否字斟句酌，因为你知道男政客与女政客受到的对待或评价是不同的。

sentences.en: I very specifically use the word contraSt.
sentences.zh: 我非常具体地使用了“对比”这个词。

sentences.en: So you were correct that I was specifically choosing those words.
sentences.zh: 所以你说得对，我确实是在字斟句酌。

sentences.en: That was your question, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是你的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's a prevailing view from Warren's supporters that Jinder was the foremost reason that she wasn't successful in this race.
sentences.zh: 沃伦的支持者中有一种普遍观点，认为性别是她在这场竞选中未能成功的最主要原因。

sentences.en: Do you share that?
sentences.zh: 你是否也这么认为？

sentences.en: You think that's a prevailing view?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是一种普遍观点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: Um, I just think I probably need more time to think about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只是觉得我可能需要更多时间来思考这个问题。

sentences.en: And I'm not trying to, like, not answer your question.
sentences.zh: 我并不是想故意不回答你的问题。

sentences.en: I think that there were what she said yesterday around, like, there were basically two ideological—I think she called them polls.
sentences.zh: 我认为正如她昨天所说的那样，基本上存在两种意识形态——我想她称之为民意测验。

sentences.en: We could call them lanes.
sentences.zh: 我们可以称之为赛道。

sentences.en: That's not necessarily genderized.
sentences.zh: 这不一定带有性别色彩。

sentences.en: That is, like, an ideological reason.
sentences.zh: 这是一个意识形态方面的原因。

sentences.en: And then I think electability, the idea of electability, was the other reason.
sentences.zh: 然后我认为胜选可能性，也就是关于胜选可能性的想法，是另一个原因。

sentences.en: Now, the idea of electability through the eyes of can a woman win?
sentences.zh: 现在，通过“女性能否获胜”这一视角来看待胜选可能性的概念，

sentences.en: Certainly, that's gender.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这就涉及性别了。

sentences.en: And I would add that it wasn't just can a woman win.
sentences.zh: 我要补充的是，这不仅仅是“女性能否获胜”。

sentences.en: It was, can a non-white or non-male candidate win?
sentences.zh: 而是“非白人或非男性候选人能否获胜？”

sentences.en: It seems—for that last point, it seems as if then this kind of place that we've ended with kind of two people on the ideological polls, both of them being, you know, white males,
sentences.zh: 对于最后一点，似乎我们最终所处的这种局面——在意识形态的两个赛道上只有两个人，而且他们都是白人男性，

sentences.en: was that inevitable?
sentences.zh: 这是不可避免的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, maybe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许吧。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It's so hard to get people—I think this is true.
sentences.zh: 让人们去理解真是太难了——我想确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, particularly being a male reporter asking women about sexism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特别是作为一个男记者去问女性关于性别歧视的问题。

sentences.en: You, like, need people to—you, like, like, oh, were you thinking about this then?
sentences.zh: 你就像是需要让人们——你就好像，哦，你当时在想这个吗？

sentences.en: And that's, like, not really how biases work, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，这其实也不是偏见起作用的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, like, does she say contrast and not attack because of sexism?
sentences.zh: 比如说，她是因为性别歧视才说对比而不是攻击吗？

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: But it's so deeply pervasive.
sentences.zh: 但它是如此根深蒂固。

sentences.en: That's not something you actively think about as you're doing it.
sentences.zh: 这不是你在做事时会有意识去想的事情。

sentences.en: And I feel like that makes sometimes the reporting challenge difficult because you're asking these candidates, like, wasn't that sexist?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有时会让报道变得很有挑战性，因为你会去问这些候选人，比如，那难道不是性别歧视吗？

sentences.en: Wasn't that racist?
sentences.zh: 那难道不是种族歧视吗？

sentences.en: Wasn't that da-da-da-da-da?
sentences.zh: 那难道不是诸如此类的话吗？

sentences.en: And it's like, maybe?
sentences.zh: 然后对方的反应就像是，也许吧？

sentences.en: I think there are a lot of challenges in the race.
sentences.zh: 我认为这次竞选面临着许多挑战。

sentences.en: And ideology was one.
sentences.zh: 意识形态就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Name recognition was one.
sentences.zh: 知名度是其中之一。

sentences.en: Fundraising is one.
sentences.zh: 筹款是其中之一。

sentences.en: And sexism and gender pervades all of those things.
sentences.zh: 而性别歧视和性别因素渗透到了所有这些事情中。

sentences.en: And does it define all of those things?
sentences.zh: 它决定了所有这些事情吗？

sentences.en: Maybe it informs all of those things is a better way to put it.
sentences.zh: 或许换个更好的说法，它影响了所有这些事情。

sentences.en: But, like, you know, how do you know?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，你怎么能知道呢？

sentences.en: Gender in this race, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这次竞选中的性别问题。

sentences.en: That is the trap question for everyone.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是对所有人的陷阱问题。

sentences.en: If you say, yeah, there was sexism in this race, everyone says, whiner.
sentences.zh: 如果你说，对，这场竞选存在性别歧视，所有人都会说，是个爱抱怨的人。

sentences.en: And if you say, no, there was no sexism, about a bazillion women think, what planet do you live on?
sentences.zh: 而如果你说，不，没有性别歧视，大概会有无数女性觉得，你到底生活在哪个星球上？

sentences.en: I promise you this.
sentences.zh: 我向你保证。

sentences.en: I will have a lot more to say on that subject later on.
sentences.zh: 关于这个主题，我以后还会有很多话要说。

sentences.en: Senator, advice to your supporters right now.
sentences.zh: 参议员，您现在对支持者有什么建议吗？

sentences.zh: 我是指，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.zh: 他们有什么过敏症或饮食禁忌吗？

sentences.zh: 他们是习惯喝咖啡还是喝茶？
